brief.headline: Energy leads, tech mixed, gold weakens as risk-on holds near highs
brief.regime_summary: SPY sits 6.5% above its 200DMA and just 0.7% above the 50DMA, essentially flat on the week (down 0.1%). VIX at 16.97 is only marginally above its 20DMA of 16.78, signaling calm but not complacency. Breadth is solid: 8 of 11 sectors trade above their 50DMAs. Sector rotation is telling: XLE leads 20-day momentum at +11.3%, while XLK is negative at -2.4% and XLC is the clear laggard at -7.1%. The regime is risk-on, but tech rotation is a headwind for growth-heavy portfolios.

portfolio.note: Price 531.01, just 0.2% above the 20DMA with RSI at 57. Momentum is positive (20-day +3.5%, 40-day +6.0%) and the MA stack is fully bullish, but MSFT sits 3.6% off its 20-day high and XLK sector momentum is negative (-2.4%). No near-term catalyst; next earnings January 2027.

Price 1,662.85 is 2.4% below the 20DMA and 11.1% off the 20-day high, with 20-day momentum at -8.1% and RS vs market at -9.4%. EPS revisions are meaningfully positive (+7.5%) and forward PE of 26.5x is reasonable, but the MA stack is mixed and the tape is not supporting the name right now. Thesis intact, but technical pressure warrants a closer look at position sizing.

XLE at 68.45 is 3.0% above the 20DMA, RSI 62, and leads all sectors on 20-day momentum (+11.3%). Still 22% below cost basis of 88.00, but price action is the best in the portfolio; energy is the strongest regime pocket this week.

GLD at 373.51 is 1.1% below its 20DMA, 3.5% below the 40DMA, and in a bearish MA stack. RSI is 42.6 and 20-day momentum is -1.9%. Gold futures (GC=F) confirm: down 2.0% vs 20DMA, RSI 37, 5.0% off 20-day high. In a risk-on regime this softness is consistent, but the drawdown from cost basis of 230 is now the only cushion; worth reviewing whether the hedging rationale still holds.

watchlist.name: Accenture plc
watchlist.thesis: ACN is up 33.8% over 20 days and 30.4% over 40 days, both by far the strongest momentum figures in the screen. Price at 243.40 is 9.4% above the 20DMA and 20.3% above the 40DMA. Trailing PE of 17.9x is only 3.5% above historical median, so valuation is not stretched relative to the move. Revenue estimates revised up 5.3%. Next earnings December 17.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA ~222, 20-day high implied ~259 (6.2% above), ATR 14% of price (high vol name, wide stops needed)
watchlist.risk: High 20-day vol of 73.3% means a one-ATR pullback is 4.3 points; a miss of the Dec earnings catalyst or a broader tech rotation could unwind the move quickly.

watchlist.name: ConocoPhillips
watchlist.thesis: COP at 149.06 is 6.5% above its 20DMA with RSI 68.8 and 20-day momentum of +19.1%. Energy is the top sector this week and COP leads within XLE. EPS estimates revised up 4.9%. PE vs history is elevated at 49% premium, which is the main valuation flag. Earnings November 5 are a near-term catalyst.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA ~140, 20-day high ~152.8 (2.4% above current), ATR ~3.5 pts (2.4% of price)
watchlist.risk: P/E at 49% premium to history limits multiple expansion; an oil price reversal or weak Q3 guidance on Nov 5 could reprice sharply.

watchlist.name: Texas Instruments
watchlist.thesis: TXN surged +8.9% this week, sitting 7.7% above the 20DMA and essentially at the 20-day high (0.05% off). RSI is 70.4, technically overbought. EPS estimates up 6.5% and 40-day momentum is +22.3%. The semiconductor cycle recovery thesis is being validated. Worth watching for a post-earnings consolidation entry rather than chasing at current levels.
watchlist.risk: RSI at 70 and price extended 7.7% above 20DMA in a sector (XLK) with negative 20-day momentum; a broader tech sell-off hits this disproportionately.

watchlist.name: Visa Inc.
watchlist.thesis: Visa at 400.60 is 2.5% above its 20DMA with a clean bullish MA stack, 11.5% 20-day momentum, and the strongest estimate revision in the screen: EPS up 13.7%, revenue up 11.6%. Consumer spending resilience underpins the setup. RS vs market is +10.2% over 20 days.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA ~391, 20-day high ~414.9 (3.6% above), ATR ~6.97 pts (1.7% of price)
watchlist.risk: Down 1.8% this week despite strong data; watch whether the weekly softness is rotation out of financials or a sign of distribution.

watchlist.name: Intel Corporation
watchlist.thesis: INTC reports earnings today (Oct 29). Price at 95.53 is 4.9% below the 20DMA, 9.4% below the 100DMA, and 24.2% off the 20-day high. 20-day momentum is -20.5% and RS vs market is -21.8%. The stock is in a clear bearish MA stack despite a +2.8% bounce this week. Forward PE of 43.9x on a recovery EPS estimate of $1.54 leaves little margin for error on today's report.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA 100.46, 20-day high 126.00 (31.9% above), ATR ~5.33 pts (5.6% of price)
watchlist.risk: An earnings beat with raised guidance could squeeze the short setup violently given the 24% drawdown from highs; position sizing matters.

watchlist.name: Bank of America
watchlist.thesis: BAC at 50.85 is 2.7% below the 20DMA and 12.8% below the 100DMA with RSI near oversold at 29.8. 20-day momentum is -6.6%, 40-day is -17.6%, and EPS estimates have been cut 4.3% in 30 days. XLF sector momentum of +5.1% is middling but BAC is lagging badly within it.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA ~52.26, 20-day high ~54.93 (8.0% above), ATR ~1.12 pts (2.2% of price)
watchlist.risk: RSI near 30 means a technical bounce is plausible; a broad market rally or rate-cut surprise would lift the whole sector and trap a short.

commodities.name: WTI Crude
commodities.note: WTI at 101.39 is 4.8% above the 20DMA with bullish MA stack and 20-day momentum of +9.2%. Up 1.9% this week. Trend is intact but price sits 8.2% off the 20-day high; watch whether it reclaims that level or rolls over.

commodities.name: Gold
commodities.note: Gold at 4,045.50 is 2.0% below its 20DMA in a bearish MA stack with RSI at 37 and momentum of -3.7% over 20 days. The risk-on regime is drawing capital away from safe havens; the key level to watch is the 20DMA near 4,130.

commodities.name: Silver
commodities.note: Silver at 52.91 is 7.6% below its 20DMA with RSI at 29.2 (oversold) and an extreme relative volume print of 18.6x normal. The 20-day high is 14.1% above current price. Heavy selling in extreme volume is a yellow flag; watch for either a capitulation low or a failed bounce.

commodities.name: Natural Gas
commodities.note: Natural gas up 8.4% this week to 3.03, 20-day momentum +2.1%, all MAs stacking bullishly. RSI is 53 so not yet overbought. High volatility (55% annualized) and thin liquidity make it a wide-stop situation.

commodities.name: Copper
commodities.note: Copper at 6.595 is essentially flat vs its 20DMA (+0.5%) with RSI 52 and modest positive momentum. Relative volume spiked to 7.5x, suggesting active repositioning. The mixed MA stack says no clear trend yet, but industrial-demand signals are worth monitoring alongside China macro news.

risks: INTC earnings today (Oct 29): forward PE of 43.9x on a recovery EPS of $1.54 means any guidance miss could see sharp downside; a beat squeezes bearish setups across legacy semi names.
COP earnings November 5: oil at $101 has lifted energy estimates, but PE at a 49% premium to history means the bar is high and any demand-outlook softness hits doubly hard.
XLK sector momentum negative at -2.4% with XLC at -7.1%: two of the largest index sectors are lagging in a risk-on tape, which could cap SPY upside even as energy and defensives run.
Silver's 18.6x relative volume in a bearish MA stack (RSI 29) signals possible forced selling or a derivatives unwind; contagion to gold and GLD is the tail risk for the portfolio hedge.
SPY is only 0.7% above its 50DMA after a flat week: if breadth narrows further and XLK does not stabilize, the index could test the 50DMA, which would shift regime signals toward neutral.
